A key may act for an agent by sending `X-AICC-Agent-ID`; the same header on a session request is refused. A mutating request that authenticates with the cookie must also carry X-AICC-Csrf; one that authenticates with a key must not — that header protects a credential the browser sends automatically.\n\nErrors always use the single envelope {\"error\": {code, message, params}}; the code is machine-readable and localized by the client. That holds for the router's own refusals too: a path this contract does not declare is 404 NOT_FOUND and a method it does not declare on a path it does is 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, both in the envelope — never the web application's index.html,
